headline: SpaceX and Super Micro beats revive the AI trade; Nasdaq +1.1% as AT&T and Netflix lag
summary: A tech-led day. The Nasdaq gained from the open on overnight AI earnings while the S&P 500 and Dow hovered near flat in the first hour, then buying broadened and the S&P 500 closed near its high for a third straight gain, within 1% of its Oct 6 record. Technology was the best sector, communication services the worst, and small caps added less than 0.5% after Tuesday's surge.
drivers: SpaceX results put the AI trade back on

SpaceX's revenue rose 161% to $14.58B, well above forecasts, and it posted its first profit as a public company as its AI compute business boomed; the stock rose 7.8%. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have set up special committees to study a merger, and Tesla gained more than 3% ahead of its own results, one of the biggest lifts to the S&P 500.

Super Micro jumped about 10% to top the S&P 500 after lifting its September-quarter sales estimate to $18.5–19.5B from a $14.5–15.5B forecast, and Dell and HPE followed. Chips extended their rebound from an eight-session slide: Nvidia rose about 2%, AMD more than 3%, and Micron and Marvell nearly 2%.

AT&T fell about 6% despite beating forecasts, on fears SpaceX will compete in mobile service, and Netflix lost about 5% after a weak fourth-quarter outlook and a cut to its ad-revenue target. Alphabet slipped, and Abbott fell about 4% after trimming its sales-growth outlook; Capital One rose about 4% on its beat.

Brent jumped more than $2 toward $111 when Iran played down hopes of talks with the US, then faded to settle flat at $108.82; WTI ended 0.7% lower at $97.15 despite a 3.1M-barrel US crude draw. The 10-year yield stayed near 5.1%, though a 20-year bond auction cleared at 5.469%, the highest since 1986.
week: Week so far: Nasdaq +2.2%, Russell 2000 +2.2%, Dow +1.6%, S&P 500 +1.3%, as chips recover part of last week's AI-led rout. Brent is still in a $97–112 range this month and the 10-year yield remains above 5% ahead of next week's Fed decision.
watch: Next: Tesla, Meta, Lam Research and Texas Instruments reported after the close and oil rose after hours on reports of an attack on Saudi Aramco; Western Digital reports Thursday, the Fed decides Oct 28 (SK hynix reports that day) and Intel follows Oct 29.
